implementations.name: Nakamura, Saito & Yoshii 2020 fingering HMMs (C++)
implementations.approach: 1st/2nd/3rd-order HMM over finger states, emission = keyboard-position interval (dx in white keys, dy black/white), -5 log-penalty for wrong-direction fingers within 30 ms, each hand separately; chord HMM (CHMM) with vertical+horizontal models
implementations.notes: Builds with MinGW g++ 9.2 unchanged. Our scorer reproduces the paper's Table 2 exactly from the authors' released outputs (Result_FHMM*.zip). Re-running the binaries on PIG v1.2 gives +0.6..0.9 points because 64 test notes changed hand between dataset versions. HMM2/3 read the hand from the SIGN of the input finger column, not the channel (the wrapper writes +1/-1 blanks).

implementations.name: Nakamura web demo FHMM1 (JavaScript)
implementations.approach: JS port of FHMM1 with parameters embedded in myfunctions.js (w1 = 1) + a hand-separation HMM for MIDI input
implementations.notes: Scores within 0.1 of the C++ FHMM1. The hand-separation HMM (HandSepModel) is reusable for MIDI input without hands.

implementations.name: marcomusy/pianoplayer 3.0.2
implementations.approach: physical hand model (finger rest positions in cm, hand size), exhaustive search over the next 5-9 notes minimising average finger speed; chords staggered into short runs
implementations.notes: Bug: its PIG reader never sets the key position INote.x (every note at x=0 -> all thumbs, and the search never finishes on real pieces); we set x with models.keypos like its MusicXML reader. 'pianoplayer' additionally staggers chord notes low->high by 0.05 s like the MusicXML/MIDI readers (= its main use case); 'pianoplayer_pigreader_nostagger' is the PIG reader as shipped (+ x fix). Its PIG reader also treats any finger already in the file as a fixed anchor (GT leak if fed a PIG file).

implementations.name: Ramoneda et al. 2022 ArGNN / ArLSTM (ACM MM)
implementations.approach: autoregressive seq2seq: pitch embedding -> 3 gated graph layers over onset/next edges (ArGNN) or 3-layer BiLSTM (ArLSTM) -> AR LSTM decoder; pretrained on ThumbSet (2523 crowd-annotated MuseScore pieces, partial labels), finetuned per hand on PIG; LH mirrored to RH
implementations.trained_on: ThumbSet + PIG official train split (031-150 minus their val)
implementations.notes: Pretrained weights ship in models/. Repository contains file names with ':' (invalid on Windows) -> sparse checkout. Inference re-uses their loader/edge code; M_gen within 0.1 of their table_beam_k.json for greedy (ArGNN 64.65 vs 64.70, ArLSTM 64.17 vs 64.25) and within 0.4 for beam 10 (66.73 vs 66.82, 65.13 vs 65.48). ThumbSet itself is 'available upon request' (Zenodo).

implementations.name: dvdrndlph/pydactyl (Randolph)
implementations.approach: classic monophonic models: Parncutt et al. 1997 (12 rules), Jacobs 2001, Badgerow 2009, Balliauw 2017 rules (in Parncutt's DP/k-best framework), Hart et al. 2000 cost table DP, random; chords arpeggiated low->high
implementations.notes: Patches: '/tmp' + ':' log path (Windows), Balliauw rule 15 AttributeError (handed_finger_* typo); python-magic stubbed. Parncutt-family raises 'No solution' when a leap exceeds every finger pair's MaxPrac and Hart's table stops at 12 semitones, so the wrapper splits the hand at large leaps (15,12,11,9,... semitones) only when needed (~12 splits/piece). Its CRF/Sayegh experiments are tied to the author's local corpus DB and were not run.

implementations.name: Kanma/piano_fingering (PyPI piano_fingering 1.0.0; port of blakewest/performer)
implementations.approach: Viterbi over per-onset chord layers with a hand-made pairwise (note1, note2, finger1, finger2) cost table per hand
implementations.notes: Runs unchanged; 0.01 s per piece.

implementations.name: thegreatkwanghyeon/autofingering
implementations.approach: Python re-implementation of Nakamura's 1st-order HMM (finger pair transitions, white/black key-distance emission)
implementations.notes: Patch: DataFrame.append -> pd.concat (pandas 2). MusicXML-only CLI, so the Hand class is called directly.

implementations.name: lumikey/piano-fingering-model
implementations.approach: ~100k-parameter Transformer encoder per hand over 26 tokens (last note of each finger, current note, 20-note lookahead with optional finger hints), greedy autoregressive decoding; ONNX + TS package for the browser
implementations.trained_on: pretrained: ALL 309 PIG files (54239 RH + 45801 LH samples = every PIG note) + other data; retrained: PIG train split only
implementations.notes: The released checkpoints saw the test pieces (score 74.1 > human agreement 71.4). Retrained on 031-150 with the repository's own train() it gets 66.2, competitive with ArGNN. Same ONNX weights are reused by JeffreyZhou798/Piano-Fingering-Generator-A09.

implementations.name: chrsztz/APF-Gen
implementations.approach: CNN-BiLSTM + local attention + AR finger embedding + auxiliary 'physical' head over hand-crafted features (beats, intervals, chord rank, hand position), 11-class signed finger output, beam search with physical transition costs
implementations.trained_on: pretrained: random 70% of the 309 PIG files (seed 42) = most test-piece annotations; retrained: PIG train split
implementations.notes: Their reported 'test' M_gen ~82% comes from a random file-level split (other annotators of the same piece in training). Only best.pt matches the released feature code; the 26 ablation checkpoints next to it have an older feature size. infer.py hard-codes device 'mps' from the config. Retrained on the official split it drops to 58.4 (beam) / 59.1 (argmax).

implementations.name: MarcAlKareh/fingerflow (FingerFlow engine)
implementations.approach: 99-feature biomechanical cost (physical key geometry, spans scaled to hand, legato coupling, speed factor, Fitts-law relocation, finger-pair indicators) + second-order Viterbi over chord-aware assignments; weights learned by averaged passive-aggressive structured perceptron with Hamming-augmented decoding
implementations.trained_on: PIG 031-150 (trained by our wrapper; repository default hyper-parameters)
implementations.notes: Best fair result. Its own benchmark claims 70.00 M_gen on the same 30 pieces (their metric code; ours gives 68.6). Their docs claim PIG timings come from real performances; PIG's README says they are synthesized from score-editing software.

implementations.name: vibetuned/chirality
implementations.approach: exact second-order Viterbi over the 12 Parncutt rule point-sums; weights uniform or learned by path-difference learning (averaged structured perceptron); also Nakamura HMM port, Jacobs/Balliauw/Al Kasimi rule sets, VNS, PPO agents
implementations.trained_on: PIG 031-150 (learned variant, trained by our wrapper with its own perceptron)
implementations.notes: Declares Python >= 3.14 / numpy >= 2.4 but the modules used run unchanged on 3.11. Exact Viterbi lifts plain Parncutt rules from 62.9 (pydactyl's pruned Dijkstra) to 65.4; learned weights 66.0. PPO agents (RH-only, 42-45%) not run.

implementations.name: V9011N/pygame-piano-animator (Hand-thesia) fingering planner
implementations.approach: beam search over chord fingerings with a physical cost model (stretch, cramp, crossings, weak fingers, black keys, shifts vs. time, finger speed) + figure templates (scales, arpeggios, octaves, thirds, trills); ~30 weights fitted by coordinate search on PIG 031-150
implementations.notes: Its MIDI/PIG loader re-orders notes; map back by (onset, pitch, channel). Strong (65.8) and fast (~0.1 s/piece).

implementations.name: emanuelemerlo/smart-piano-fingering (MuseScore 4 plugin)
implementations.approach: QML/JavaScript port + extension of pianoplayer's hand model (chord & multi-voice handling, held-note constraints, exact DP when feasible)
implementations.notes: Core sliced out of the .qml and run in Node exactly like its own tests (MuseScore not needed). Beat = 0.5 s assumed. Clearly better than pianoplayer itself (58.8 vs 57.2).

implementations.name: BShakhovsky/PianoFingering_CalcModule (of PianoTranscription_Windows)
implementations.approach: trellis graph over chord fingering combinations with vertical (in-chord) and horizontal (1-3 chord) cost rules, keeping all min-cost paths
implementations.notes: MSVC-only C++; built with MinGW g++ 9.2 via a force-included compat header ('abstract' keyword), a 5-line boost::noncopyable stand-in and patches/bshakhovsky.patch (i16 literal, pure-virtual destructor with body, #pragma comment).

implementations.name: carlosrmz009/OpenNote (Rust)
implementations.approach: Viterbi over a biomechanical hand model + union of published rule sets (Parncutt, Jacobs, Balliauw, Badgerow; 'consensus' weighting) + optional learned n-gram prior
implementations.trained_on: none (rules only; the learned prior is not distributed)
implementations.notes: Official builds embed models/helios-beta1.8.json (absent from the repo); published models are sealed for official builds. No MSVC linker -> built with the GNU Rust toolchain. Repo is 1.4 GB (videos) -> sparse checkout.

implementations.name: huukhangapcs/AutomaticPianoFingering
implementations.approach: phrase detection + motif/pattern library (Alberti, arpeggios hard-locked) + phrase-scoped Viterbi over 5-finger hand states with 3-D key geometry; 'simple' pipeline = plain physics DP
implementations.notes: README claims 85.53% accuracy (own metric, first 20 PIG files); on the PIG test protocol the full phrase-aware pipeline scores 45.7 and the simple DP 59.9.

implementations.name: jpsmith8488/valhala-fingering-solver (ValHaLA)
implementations.approach: first-order Viterbi over a 14-term physical 'action' (kinetic, topographic, gravity, collision, coupling, key action, adhesion, tempo, rotation, tradition, ...), monophonic and isochronous
implementations.notes: Its BilateralSolver fingers the left hand with the right-hand model (no mirroring) -> 31.5. Mirroring LH pitches (our modification) -> 52.3.

implementations.name: JuliaMusic/PianoFingering.jl (Gao et al. 2023, Applied Sciences)
implementations.approach: model-based RL: each hand split into segments, each segment an MDP with rule-based rewards, solved with Dyna-Q (10,000 episodes) in parallel threads; greedy policy = fingering
implementations.notes: Portable Julia 1.10.5, PyCall bound to the baselines venv (music21). Its PIG reader takes the hand from the finger SIGN. Crashes on 4/30 test pieces (022, 026, 028, 030: states without any legal action). Score is over the 26 pieces it finished.

implementations.name: Balliauw, Herremans et al. 2017 VNS (C++)
implementations.approach: variable neighbourhood search (swap/change/split-part moves, tabu list, perturbations) over a 15-rule polyphonic cost (Parncutt-derived + chord rules)
implementations.notes: Fragile MusicXML importer (start times recomputed from voice durations, ties ignored); we generate a compatible single-measure MusicXML on a rank time axis (one 'slice' per division, so an absolute grid is very slow). Patch: -seed for reproducibility. The released code (HEAD 2014-11-06, default parameters) does not reach good solutions: on its own bundled example piece2.xml the returned fingering repeats fingers on consecutive different notes (right-hand cost 60877); on PIG 008 the search plateaus after a 7% cost reduction from its random start; with the 'events' time axis rest slices break the slice-adjacency rules (right-hand cost 0). Stopped after 12/30 test pieces (5 min/piece on average), M_gen below random. Nakamura et al. 2020 report 56.7 M_gen for the authors' own run on 14 pieces.

implementations.name: TimKoornstra/automatic-piano-fingering
implementations.approach: tabular Q-learning over (prev, current, next note) with a toy reward (distance to the finger's slot in a rigid hand frame)
implementations.notes: RH-only upstream; LH mirrored by us; notes clipped into its Q-table range.

implementations.name: ackyedy/piano-fingering-analysis
implementations.approach: semitone-interval HMMs (order 1, interpolated order 2) + baselines (most frequent finger, direction rule)
implementations.notes: Semitone intervals (no black/white key geometry) lose ~2-5 points vs Nakamura's key-position HMMs.

implementations.name: CHOWMHALVIN/Piano-Fingering-Suggestion-Model-with-Intuitive-UI
implementations.approach: first-order HMM (white/black key distance emission) + hand-size leap limits, chord penalties, scale thumb rules in the Viterbi pass
implementations.trained_on: PIG 031-150 (trained by our wrapper; repo uses a random 80/20 piece split)
implementations.notes: The repository also redistributes PIG v1.2 (used by the datasets agent as a mirror).

implementations.name: anandaphan/EER-piano-fingering (Iman & Ahn 2025, Mathematics)
implementations.approach: per-piece model-free RL: factored dueling DQN with Elite Episode Replay, reward = Parncutt-style rules (3,4,12,...)
implementations.trained_on: none, but the first chord of each hand is fixed to annotator 1's ground truth (piece_details.npy)
implementations.notes: Runs (gym 0.26.2 + torch 2.5.1) but ~28 s per episode on piece 002 -> the default 500 episodes x 2 hands is ~8 h per piece; only 5 test pieces (002,016,017,025,026) are in its bundled table. Stopped after 32 episodes; not scored.
